title: Harmanpreet Singh Hat-Trick Powers India to 4-2 Win Over Malaysia
excerpt: The captain scored in the 3rd, 33rd and 58th minutes in Jalandhar as India made it four straight wins at the Asian Champions Trophy and stayed top of the standings.
body:
• India beat Malaysia 4-2 in Jalandhar on Sunday for a fourth straight win at the men's Asian Champions Trophy, staying unbeaten at the top of the standings.
  • Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored a hat-trick — penalty corners in the 3rd and 33rd minutes and a penalty stroke in the 58th — and was named Player of the Match.
  • Sukhjeet Singh added India's third goal in the 43rd minute; Akhimullah Anuar (25th) and Shello Silverius (60th) scored for Malaysia.
  • India, already into the semi-finals, play South Korea in their final round-robin match on Monday, November 2.

India made it four wins from four at the Asian Champions Trophy on Sunday, beating Malaysia 4-2 at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar behind a hat-trick from captain Harmanpreet Singh. The result kept the five-time champions unbeaten and top of the standings with 12 points from four matches and a goal difference of +21, according to IANS.

The match was a rematch of the Asian Games gold-medal game, where India beat Malaysia 5-1. Both teams had already secured semi-final places before Sunday, alongside South Korea and Japan, The Bridge reported.

Harmanpreet sets the tone, then settles it

Harmanpreet opened the scoring in the third minute, converting India's first penalty corner with a flick to the left of Malaysian goalkeeper Hafizuddin Othman. Malaysia levelled in the 25th minute through Akhimullah Anuar, but Harmanpreet restored the lead from another penalty corner in the 33rd minute.

https://x.com/TheHockeyIndia/status/2116921828916805673

Sukhjeet Singh extended the lead in the 43rd minute with a field goal, set up after vice-captain Hardik Singh won the ball in midfield. India then survived a spell with Harmanpreet off the field, before the captain completed his hat-trick in the 58th minute: his goal-bound flick from a penalty corner struck a Malaysian defender on the goal line, and he converted the resulting penalty stroke. Silverius pulled one back in the final minute for Malaysia, but the result was already settled.

Harmanpreet was named Player of the Match. Reports differed on his tournament tally — IANS put him at the top of the scoring chart with eight goals, while The Bridge's match report counted six — but both agreed he leads the tournament's scorers.

What it means

India's earlier wins in the tournament came against Bangladesh (13-0), China (5-2) and Japan (4-1). Malaysia remain second in the standings despite the defeat. With the semi-final line-up already decided, Monday's final round-robin matches are about seeding: India face South Korea, while Malaysia play Japan.

For Indian fans in North America, the knockout rounds later this week are the matches that matter — India have won every game so far, but the title will be decided in the semi-finals and final, not the group table.
